results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. 

VFB holds extensive data related to the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body, with over 600 records of neurons and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004952,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") records of parts. Additionally, there are images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body and expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells, including gamma Kenyon cells. According to the VFB database, there are three main subtypes that project their axons to different lobes: alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, as referenced in Lee et al., 1999, and Aso et al., 2014. The VFB database also holds specific information on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression.

results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, which feed reward or punishment information into the mushroom body. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. VFB holds extensive data on adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, including [2415](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") images, [21](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") subclasses, [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") scRNAseq datasets, [64](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") transgene expression records, [316](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") downstream connectivity classes, and [1290](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") upstream connectivity classes.

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") Kenyon cells is acetylcholine. This information comes from the VFB database, which supports [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") as cholinergic, i.e. using acetylcholine, based on VFB neurotransmitter tags obtained through the VFB query.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which states that any antennal lobe projection neuron sends synaptic output to the mushroom body, and that these neurons generally project to the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. Additionally, the [antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is not explicitly mentioned in the available data as a connecting region, but the general connection pattern of the antennal lobe to higher brain centers is described. VFB holds data on 24 brain regions, and for the antennal lobe, it has information on its connections to other regions, including the mushroom body.

results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila central brain contains approximately more than 125,000 neurons, according to the Virtual Fly Brain database, as determined by the VFB query. results.title: Central complex structure

results.response:
The main components of the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge, as stated in the VFB database. VFB holds a range of data related to the adult central complex, including images, neuron information, parts of the complex, and transgene expression data, with for example, [13781](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in adult central complex") images of neurons with some part in the adult central complex and [86](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult central complex") instances of transgene expression in the adult central complex.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type has an ID of [1813403998](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open 1813403998 in Virtual Fly Brain"). It is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer. The dendritic arbor extends outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. LPLC2 detects looming, or expansion, stimuli. This neuron type has connections to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. 

VFB holds information on over 20,000 neurons, including LPLC2. The available data on LPLC2 is based on information from Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017, which is summarized in the VFB database.

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult Drosophila is more elaborated than in larval Drosophila. According to VFB, the adult antennal lobe has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas the larval antennal lobe has around 22 glomeruli (VFB, VFB). This suggests a significant difference in the complexity of the antennal lobe between adult and larval Drosophila. VFB holds data on the [antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), but the provided evidence does not specify how this neuron contributes to the organisation of the antennal lobe in adult versus larval Drosophila.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response:
Based on the available evidence from VFB, it is suggested that adult visual projection neurons might mediate the connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"), as they have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This is supported by the claim from VFB that "adult visual projection neurons to the mushroom body have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body" (VFB). 

While the question asks about [visual system neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") and [adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB holds relevant data on these neuron types, including their downstream and upstream connectivity classes, which could be used to further investigate potential connections between the visual system and the mushroom body. For example, VFB has downstream connectivity classes for visual system neuron ([6768](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for visual system neuron") records) and upstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron ([1290](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") records), which might provide insights into the potential pathways through which visual information could reach the memory circuit. 

However, the literature does not provide a direct link between visual system neuron and adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron in the provided evidence. Further analysis of the available connectivity data and other evidence would be necessary to fully understand the potential connections between these neuron types and how visual information might reach the memory circuit.

results.title: Comparative analysis
results.question: Compare the downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons (s-LNv and l-LNv). Do they converge on any common target neuron types?
results.response: The downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons, [s-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrchk8e1 "Open s-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") and [l-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fws "Open l-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain"), have been compared. According to the VFB database, s-LNv and l-LNv have downstream targets and converge on common target neuron types. These common target neuron types include adult interneurons, cholinergic neurons, GABAergic neurons, glutamatergic neurons, octopaminergic neurons, dopaminergic neurons, and serotonergic neurons. Specifically, the downstream targets of s-LNv include adult cholinergic neurons, adult octopaminergic neurons, and adult serotonergic neurons, while the downstream targets of l-LNv include neurons, adult neurons, and adult CNS neurons. VFB holds relevant data on s-LNv, including [49](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_jrchk8e1,SimilarMorphologyTo "Run in VFB: Find similar neurons to s-LNv") records of similar neurons, [75](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_jrchk8e1,NeuronNeuronConnectivityQuery "Run in VFB: Neurons connected to s-LNv") records of neurons connected to s-LNv, and [21](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_jrchk8e1,SimilarMorphologyToNB "Run in VFB: NeuronBridge matches for s-LNv") NeuronBridge matches.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response: The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is such that thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers, including mushroom-body-associated dopaminergic neurons and gamma main Kenyon cells, according to VFB downstream class-connectivity previews. This suggests that temperature information could indeed influence memory formation, as the mushroom body is involved in olfactory associative learning and memory, and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The mushroom body's calyx receives sensory interneuron afferents, and neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body provide additional inputs. VFB holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047228,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047228,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047228,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body") expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body, which could be used to further investigate the relationship between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body.
